column1: # cracking-rosetta | data/mdxfind-case-insensitive.tsv
# TYPE <TAB> reason
# mdxfind types whose recovered PLAINTEXT may differ from the stored one in
# case alone, because the type upper- or lower-cases its input before hashing.
# verify-vectors.pl relaxes its plaintext comparison on case for these types
# and for no others.
# WHY THIS IS A LIST AND NOT A FLAG. john publishes FMT_CASE -- bit 0 of
# formats.h, SET when the format IS case-sensitive -- and verify-vectors.pl
# reads it straight out of data/tools/john.yaml, so john's half of this
# problem needs no file. mdxfind's inventory carries no equivalent bit, so
# the only honest alternative to a list is a guess. Every line here therefore
# names WHAT WAS MEASURED, and a type is added only after the measurement.
# WHAT THIS FILE MUST NOT BECOME. Relaxing on case is a real weakening of the
# comparison: it accepts a plaintext that is not the string the wordlist held.
# It is legitimate only where the type makes the difference by construction --
# where no input could have produced the stored case. Do NOT add a type
# because a vector "nearly" matched; that is searching for something that
# passes, which is the same error as re-casing an upper-case digest until it
# loads.
MD5LM
column2: MD5LM is md5(LM($p)) and LM upper-cases its input before the outer md5, so the plaintext mdxfind recovers is upper case BY CONSTRUCTION and no input could have produced the stored lower-case form. Measured 2026-09-06 against three builds -- installed 1.545, local 1.576 and local 1.579 -- all three returning ROSETTA where md5-lm-plain stores rosetta. The row had sat at tier vector from an earlier, laxer pass and a strict re-verification refused it; this is what makes the strict comparison and the row agree again.
